bullets.title: Fed's Warsh signals openness to September rate hike; Invesco sees Fed at neutral
bullets.body: FT reports Fed Chair Warsh plans to stick with lean/hawkish messaging despite market backlash and is open to raising rates in September if inflation data surprises to the upside. Invesco argues the Fed is not behind the curve, estimating neutral at 3.5%-4.0%, roughly consistent with the current 3.50%-3.75% policy range. Trump has spoken repeatedly with Warsh since his appointment, a departure from recent practice.

bullets.title: Labor market remains strong: jobless claims 199K (3rd sub-200K print), layoffs plunge 46% YoY
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims came in at 199K vs. 203K expected, the third consecutive reading below 200K, with the four-week moving average also sub-200K. Challenger July job cuts plunged 46.1% YoY and 27% MoM to 33,429—the lowest monthly total in three years. Q2 productivity rose 1.4% QoQ AR (vs. 0.6% consensus) while unit labor costs climbed just 1.3% QoQ AR, supporting benign inflation and consumer income outlook. July NFP consensus sits around +80K.

bullets.title: Hormuz Strait reopening deal imminent; oil higher on optimism
bullets.body: Tehran and Muscat have reportedly reached broad agreement on a temporary Hormuz transit corridor, with a formal joint statement expected within days. The proposed deal spans 60 days and still requires Iran's security council approval. Oil and yields are both higher in response; Brent crude was up ~1% to $80/bbl in pre-market. UBS energy flow data confirms Hormuz flows remain at low levels with Bab el Mandeb also declining.

bullets.title: Tech HF losses hit record -10% in July; semis/memory liquidation dominated
bullets.body: TMT-dedicated hedge funds suffered their worst monthly drawdown on record at -10.2% in July; multi-strat funds lost 2.3% (fourth-worst ever). Losses were driven by concentrated positions in semis/memory, mishandled vol/correlation in options, and inadequate liquidity stress-testing. The Situational Awareness fund saw AUM collapse from $45B to $10B. Tech rally is now more dependent on retail flows and leveraged ETFs, increasing volatility. SOXL saw its sixth-largest MOC buying imbalance (~$8.5B) in its history.

bullets.title: AI capex/ROI concerns re-emerging as risk-on/risk-off factor; hyperscaler CDS widening
bullets.body: Bloomberg and Morgan Stanley note AI sector concerns around elevated capex, ROI, and circular financing—which had dissipated—are returning and the market is treating AI as a macro risk-on/risk-off factor. Hyperscaler CDS spreads moved wider following Alphabet's 10-part investment-grade bond offering. MS projects $1.4T in AI capex with 25-50% GenAI ROIC across three business models; SpaceX reportedly guided $100B 2026 exit revenue on a 4x Nvidia compute ramp (2GW to 8+GW).

bullets.title: GOOGL talent exodus to Discovery Loop raises frontier model credibility concerns
bullets.body: Jeff Dean and three Google AI executives departed to launch the Discovery Loop startup, sending GOOGL down ~4%. Demis Hassabis is stepping down as DeepMind CEO to Chief Scientist, refocusing on Isomorphic Labs. GOOGL researchers are frustrated by compute being diverted to TPU sales vs. internal R&D, with talent flowing to OpenAI and Anthropic. Gemini 4 is reportedly on track but GOOGL's frontier model status is increasingly in question, even as the GCP/infrastructure business shows strong customer momentum.

bullets.title: Software sentiment mixed: SHOP/DASH break out, HUBS/APP/DDOG disappoint sharply
bullets.body: Earnings divergence is sharp in software: SHOP surged 17% on 33% revenue growth and AI acceleration (Citi PT raised to $196); DASH +4% on biggest EBITDA beat in 2+ years with US restaurant GOV +17% and Q3 EBITDA guide 10% above consensus. HUBS fell ~24% after cutting FY guidance, with net new customer adds at lowest since Q1 2020 and NRR ticking to 102%—Wolfe downgraded to Peer Perform guiding FY27 growth to 13% vs. consensus 15%. DDOG dropped 17% as Q3 revenue guide implies deceleration to +28-29% from +36%. APP fell 19% on its first revenue miss in 14 quarters with compute costs accelerating and install volumes negative for four consecutive quarters.

bullets.title: Memory complex under pressure: WDC -13%, SNDK -7% despite strong quarters; expectations too high
bullets.body: Goldman TMT notes both SanDisk and Western Digital traded down after hours despite strong results, attributing the move to elevated buy-side expectations rather than fundamental deterioration. SNDK beat on revenue/margin/EPS but Q3 guide missed by 5%; it has signed 8 New Business Models covering ~50% of FY27 bits and ~66% of FY28 bits at floor pricing. WDC gross margin expanded to 54.4% but exabyte shipments lagged due to 40TB ePMR product transition. Citi maintains Buy on both: SNDK PT $2,100, WDC PT $740. Analysts prefer STX, which guided 14% QoQ revenue growth vs. WDC's 9% with superior HAMR technology positioning.

bullets.title: Broad market near flat; S&P 500 at 7,712, VIX at 15.31; market broadening to highest in 10 years
bullets.body: S&P 500 is up 0.1% to 7,712.53 with VIX at 15.31 (+3.2%). Nasdaq futures are slipping on tech earnings-driven anxiety. JPM notes 57% of SPY constituents are beating the index, the highest breadth reading in 10 years. Russell 2000 is up 21.6% YTD, outperforming S&P by 8.8%, with aggregate earnings 9.4% above expectations. Info tech is trading at 20x post-July selloff, a one-year low vs. the 10-year average of 23x. AAII bullish sentiment improved to 37% (highest in 3 weeks) with bull-bear spread at -1%.

bullets.title: TSMC sitting on $1B Apple A20 Pro SoCs due to DRAM bottleneck
bullets.body: TSMC reportedly holds approximately $1B worth of Apple A20 Pro SoCs that cannot advance to the next production stage due to insufficient DRAM supply. The bottleneck suggests DRAM supply constraints are creating ripple effects across the semiconductor supply chain beyond memory names directly.

bullets.title: Alphabet kicks off 10-part investment-grade bond offering; Treasuries fall on Warsh report
bullets.body: Alphabet launched a 10-part US dollar investment-grade bond sale, with hyperscaler CDS spreads widening in response. Treasuries declined following the Warsh hawkish-lean report, with 10-year yields at 4.64-4.65% (+2-3 bps) and 2-year at 4.204% (+2.5 bps). MUFG sees the dollar as still undervalued against 8 of 9 G10 currencies, with geopolitical risk premium remaining priced in.

bullets.title: Key macro data next week: CPI Aug 12, PPI Aug 13, Retail Sales Aug 14
bullets.body: JPM's macro calendar flags the most important data cluster of the month: CPI and real average hourly earnings on Aug 12, PPI on Aug 13, and retail sales on Aug 14. These prints will be critical for the September Fed meeting (Sep 16) and for determining whether Warsh's hawkish lean is validated. Chase card tracker already shows spending decelerated to 3.8% YoY in July vs. 6.0% in June, with durable goods growth collapsing to 1.0% MTD.

bullets.title: SpaceX/Tesla Terafab chip fab announced; SPCX lockup of 911.5M shares begins today
bullets.body: SpaceX and Tesla announced Terafab, a $16.8B chip fabrication facility in Grimes County, Texas targeting 1 terawatt of combined compute. Intel joined the project in April 2026. Separately, SpaceX faces a massive share unlock today of up to 911.5M shares (6.9% of outstanding), and SpaceX guidance reportedly calls for $100B 2026 exit revenue on a 4x Nvidia compute ramp. Neocloud stocks face near-term pressure from SpaceX capacity announcement.

bullets.title: FCC eliminates 39% broadcast TV ownership cap; Hormuz-threatened Starlink selloff in tower stocks seen as overdone
bullets.body: The FCC voted to eliminate the 39% national broadcast TV ownership cap, shifting to case-by-case review for deals exceeding the threshold—a clear positive for FOXA and NXST M&A optionality. Separately, Citi argues the ~5% selloff in tower stocks (AMT, SBAC, CCI) on SpaceX mobile network fears is overdone, as SpaceX may still use macro cell sites on towers and telcos (T, VZ) face greater long-term risk.

bullets.title: AI cost discipline emerging as competitive edge; model routing and token optimization key theme
bullets.body: Across multiple earnings calls, companies are embedding AI model routing strategies to manage token costs: BKNG uses routing for simple vs. complex tasks, DASH uses Dash Bench tools, NOW optimizes across frontier models. DeepSeek is reportedly planning substantial price increases, reversing the cheap-Chinese-model narrative and validating AI monetization pricing discipline. META launched Muse Code beta based on Muse Spark 1.2, narrowing the gap to frontier labs.

bullets.title: Saudi Aramco cuts Asia OSP by 50¢/bbl; copper near record highs; uranium bull case intact
bullets.body: Saudi Aramco set September Arab Light OSP at a $2/bbl discount to the regional benchmark for Asia, cutting 50¢/bbl MoM, and at -$2.15/bbl to ICE Brent for NW Europe—reflecting soft demand. LME copper climbed 1.5% to $14,316/ton on US tariff concerns and improved sentiment. BofA raised its 2027 uranium price forecast to $130/lb (~52% upside from spot) on tight supply and growing nuclear demand, with utility contract coverage declining to 48% from 56%.

bullets.title: High-beta momentum crash of July 2026 not over; long gold/short high-beta working
bullets.body: Multiple strategists flag the July 2026 high-beta momentum drawdown as ongoing with no clear reversal signal. Gold is breaking out of a two-month consolidation on dollar weakness, yield compression, and 14-day streak of China ETF inflows. The long gold / short high-beta momentum factor strategy has been working. Analysts advise booking some gold gains ahead of Friday's NFP print given hawkish risk.

bullets.title: RDDT and NYT facing structural headwinds from Google AI Overviews cannibalizing search referrals
bullets.body: Both Reddit and NYT saw inbound search traffic decline due to Google AI Overviews, with RDDT search referrals described as 'choppy.' Citi notes SEO pressure persists across RDDT and BKNG from the same source, with the impact not yet offset by broader ecosystem value. This is an emerging structural headwind for ad-supported and traffic-dependent media models.

bullets.title: Data center power constraints intensifying; Batch Zero delay benefits on-site power (SEI, BE) over IPPs
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd views the Texas Batch Zero delay as temporary (1-3 months) and bullish for on-site power providers (SEI, BE, INIO), with negative marginal impact on IPPs (VST, CEG, NRG). On-site power solutions trading at $2.09-$5.88/watt vs. a $15/watt REIT endgame. FCC targeting a ban on Chinese optical transceivers (Innolight, Eoptolink) by year-end, with Beijing signaling retaliation via indium phosphide export restrictions affecting Coherent and Lumentum.

bullets.title: Fiserv major guide-cut: FY26 EPS slashed to $7.20-7.40 from $8.00-8.30 on Argentina macro and client delays
bullets.body: FISV Q2 missed on revenue ($4.96B vs. $5.05B est.) and EPS ($1.84 vs. $1.91 est.), then cut its FY26 organic revenue guidance to -1% to 0% from +1% to +3% and adj. EPS guidance by ~10%. Management attributed headwinds to Argentina macro, hardware timing, client ramp delays, and divestitures—characterizing none as structural. A $100M incremental tech investment in H2 2026 and a portfolio review with potential divestitures were announced.
